no_english_bachelor.statement: No English-taught bachelor exists at the Faculty of Informatics; the Czech-taught Informatics (Informatika) programme is recorded instead.
no_english_bachelor.quote_1: Currently, there is no bachelor study program in English, therefore there is no entry exam to pardon.
no_english_bachelor.quote_2_context: Heading of the 'Bachelor's' block on the FI 'Programmes offered' page, which lists Informatics, Programming and Development, Cybersecurity, Bioinformatics, Informatics in Education, Business Informatics, Statistical Data Science.

programme.how_found: Search 'Masaryk University Faculty of Informatics bachelor programme Informatics English site:muni.cz' -> is.muni.cz/program/22955/informatics (blocked by a JavaScript challenge) -> opened the same programme id on the MU central catalogue, muni.cz/en/bachelors-and-masters-study-programmes/22955-informatics. FI 'Programmes offered' page: fi.muni.cz/admission/index.html.en -> link 'Entrance exam waiver' -> entry-exam-pardon.html.en.

value.description: Programme is Czech-taught. MU states that 'a serious working knowledge of Czech is required' for Czech-taught programmes, but publishes no CEFR level, no certificate list and no test. No language certificate is part of the FI bachelor admission procedure, which is decided solely by the TSP aptitude test (whose second sub-test is 'a reasoning test in English').

english.quote: Whereas students in programmes taught in English are charged very affordable fees, programmes taught in Czech are completely tuition free, but a serious working knowledge of Czech is required.
english.how_found: Search 'site:muni.cz tuition fees Czech-taught programmes free of charge foreign applicants bachelor TSP in English' -> MU 'Tuition fees and financial aid' page, section 'Programmes taught in Czech'.
english.notes: The requirement is Czech proficiency, not English, because the only FI bachelor programmes are Czech-taught. No minimum level is published anywhere found (checked FI info-bachelor 2027/28 page in English and Czech, FI admission guide, FI FAQ, MU how-to-apply, MU language-courses page). The FI 2027/28 conditions say the TSP 'consists of three separate tests: (1) a numerical and analytical reasoning test, (2) a reasoning test in English, and (3) a critical thinking test' (fi.muni.cz/admission/info-bachelor.html.en); no Czech certificate is requested. MU recommends a preparatory Czech course one year before enrolment.

value.description: No GPA/grade minimum. Admission is by the MU Study Aptitude Test (TSP, Test studijních předpokladů): pass threshold is a result in the numerical-analytical reasoning sub-test among the top 30 per cent MU-wide; ranking by the combined result of all three sub-tests. Exemption from the TSP can be requested for single-subject programmes (conditions published only in Czech).

gpa.quote: To pass the entrance examination, an applicant must achieve a result in the numerical and analytical reasoning subtest that places them amongst the top 30 per cent across the whole of Masaryk University.
gpa.how_found: fi.muni.cz/admission/index.html.en -> link 'Information about the admission procedure' -> info-bachelor.html.en ('Bachelor's degree programmes 2027/2028', approved by the FI Academic Senate on 24 June 2026).
gpa.notes: Czech original: 'Pro úspěšné složení přijímací zkoušky je požadován výsledek v subtestu numericko-analytického myšlení mezi 30% nejlepších v rámci celé MU.' Estimated intake for single-subject Informatics: 350. The MU catalogue page for the programme shows 'Admission requirements: No information available' and links a PDF 'Minimum score and numbers of accepted applicants in past years' (not read). Exemption (waiver) conditions for Czech-taught bachelor programmes are on the Czech version of entry-exam-pardon.html; the English version only says no English bachelor exists. Exemption requests must be uploaded by 28 February 2027 (FI FAQ).

deadline.how_found: fi.muni.cz/admission/index.html.en -> 'Information about the admission procedure' -> info-bachelor.html.en; cross-checked on fi.muni.cz/admission/timeline.html.en ('Key dates for the admissions process for Bachelor's programmes commencing in the 2027/2028 academic year') and fi.muni.cz/admission/guide.html.en ('from 1 November 2026 to 28 February 2027').
deadline.notes: This is the published 2027/28 (autumn 2027) cycle, not a carry-over from 2026. Czech original: 'Termíny pro podávání přihlášek: 1. 11. 2026 – 28. 2. 2027'. Application fee 900 CZK (FI guide). TSP attempt windows: 29 Nov 2026 – 14 Feb 2027 and 15 Feb – 25 Apr 2027. Proof of secondary education mid-May – mid-June 2027; admission decision by end of June 2027; online enrolment first half of July 2027. The MU central how-to-apply page lists a generic FI 'September intake: 30 April' which contradicts the FI page; the FI faculty page is the authoritative, year-specific source.

value.academic_year: not year-specific (MU rule for all Czech-taught programmes, page read 2026-10-17; applies to 2027/28 unless changed)

tuition.quote: Whereas students in programmes taught in English are charged very affordable fees, programmes taught in Czech are completely tuition free, but a serious working knowledge of Czech is required.
tuition.how_found: Search 'site:muni.cz tuition fees Czech-taught programmes free of charge ...' -> MU 'Tuition fees and financial aid' page, section 'Programmes taught in Czech'. Also programme page -> link 'Tuition fees and financial aid'.
tuition.notes: Czech-taught programme, so no tuition for any nationality. FI's own international page confirms: 'Tuition fee for Master´s degree programmes taught in English is 4,500 Eur per year, studying in the Czech language is free of charge.' (fi.muni.cz/students/international-studies/admission.html.en). For comparison, the MU fee table lists Faculty of Informatics English-taught master's at 4,500 EUR per year. Non-tuition costs: TSP/application fee 900 CZK; verification of foreign secondary education 900 CZK from 1 Sep 2025 (fi.muni.cz/admission/verification.html.en).

value.name: Accommodation scholarship (MU scholarship programme to support student accommodation, MU Measure No. 7/2025; Czech: Stipendium na podporu ubytování / ubytovací stipendium)

scholarship_exists.quote: The purpose of this scholarship programme is to provide accommodation grants to students of Masaryk University. The scholarship program to support student accommodation is announced by MU Measure No. 7/2025.
scholarship_exists.how_found: MU 'Tuition fees and financial aid' page -> section 'Financial aid' -> '2. Accommodation scholarship'; FI scholarship page fi.muni.cz/students/scholarship.html.en -> link 'university accommodation scholarship' -> muni.cz accommodation-support-scholarship page.
scholarship_exists.notes: University-run, paid each semester to enrolled students who confirm eligibility in IS MU (1–30 November for autumn, 15 March–15 April for spring); a first-year student can therefore be considered in November of the first semester. Published criteria (MU tuition page): full-time degree programme; first degree programme at any Czech university; within standard length of study; no permanent address in the Statutory City of Brno. Alternatives checked and rejected for this Czech-taught programme: 'MU Newcomers´ scholarship' (listed on the FI page, link returns 404; search snippets describe it as 100,000 CZK for programmes taught in languages other than Czech and only for selected countries) and FI's 'scholarship to support promising foreign students of English study programmes (600 EUR per semester)'. FI's 'merit scholarship for excellence (up to 18,000 CZK ~ 740 EUR per semester)' is for enrolled students on results. FI Dean's Directive 8/2025 (scholarship programmes) and MU Measure 7/2025 are on is.muni.cz and could not be read (JavaScript challenge / login).

scholarship_international.quote: Our faculty offers scholarships to full-time student during their studies, as accommodation scholarships, merit-based scholarship, scholarship to support the studies, scholarship for short-term study or internships abroad, etc.
scholarship_international.how_found: fi.muni.cz/admission/index.html.en -> master's 'Tuition' link -> fi.muni.cz/students/international-studies/admission.html.en (FI page addressed to international applicants), section 'Scholarship'.
scholarship_international.notes: Evidence is indirect but official: the FI page written for international applicants lists accommodation scholarships among what full-time students receive, and the MU eligibility criteria (full-time, first degree in CR, standard length, no permanent address in Brno-město) contain no nationality or residence-in-CR condition; the Czech FAQ (muni.cz/portal-pro-studujici/.../kdy-vznika-narok-na-ubytovaci-stipendium) repeats the same four conditions. No sentence saying 'open to foreign students' in those words was found; the governing MU Measure 7/2025 section 5 is behind the IS MU login. Payment requires a CZK current account at a bank in the Czech Republic.

access_notes: is.muni.cz (MU information system) serves a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge to non-browser clients: is.muni.cz/program/22955/informatics (both languages), is.muni.cz/prihlaska/faq.pl and the FI Dean's Directive 8/2025 PDF returned only the challenge page; not bypassed. The programme was therefore documented from the MU central catalogue page on muni.cz, which carries the same programme id 22955.
MU Measure No. 7/2025 (accommodation scholarship conditions, section 5) is linked only to is.muni.cz/auth/ (login required); eligibility was taken from the public muni.cz summary pages instead.

The FI English admission pages are labelled 'Translated using Machine-translated page for increased accessibility for English questioners. Page in original, Czech language.' The Czech original (info-bachelor.html.cs) was read and matches; key Czech sentences are given in notes.
https://www.muni.cz/en/admissions/bachelors-and-masters-studies/deadlines returned 404; deadlines are on the how-to-apply page (#ApplicationDeadlines) and on the FI timeline page.

The FI scholarship page's link 'MU Newcomers´ scholarship' (muni.cz/.../tuition-fees-and-financial-aid/newcomers-scholarships) returned 'PAGE NOT FOUND'; the scholarship could not be verified on muni.cz and in any case is described (search snippets, faculty pages) as limited to programmes taught in languages other than Czech.

Requesting the Czech page fi.muni.cz/admission/entry-exam-pardon.html via the fetch tool returned the English text; the bachelor TSP waiver conditions (Czech only) were therefore not read. The English version states that no English-taught bachelor exists.

Foreign secondary diploma (Kazakhstan): MU/FI require either general recognition (nostrification) by a Regional Authority or faculty verification under MU Directive 2/2019 (900 CZK), with certified translations into Czech or English; documents due by enrolment, FI timeline mid-May – mid-June 2027 (muni.cz verification-of-the-condition-for-admission; fi.muni.cz/admission/verification.html.en).
Budget used: 9 web searches, 33 page fetches (including 5 blocked/404/empty).
